name: Does optimizing a PDF upload my file to a server?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every page is rendered, cropped, and rebuilt entirely in your browser. Your file is never sent anywhere.

name: Will the text still be selectable or searchable afterward?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — the output is a rasterized, image-based PDF, the same trade-off PDFree's Clean Scan tool makes. Cropping and reflowing a real fixed-layout PDF without turning it into images isn't reliably possible; if you need to keep selectable text, don't run it through this tool.

name: How does the automatic margin detection work?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree samples pages across the document, detects each one's actual content area, and takes the median across those samples — so a single full-bleed photo or a near-blank divider page can't drag the crop box too tight or too loose for the rest of the book.

name: Which devices are the presets tuned for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kindle (6"/7" screens), reMarkable and Onyx Boox (10.3" screens), and Kobo/Nook readers. Each preset matches the target device's screen aspect ratio so pages fill the screen without letterboxing more than necessary.

name: Could this crop off real content, like a footnote near the edge?

acceptedAnswer.text: The crop only ever grows outward from the detected content box toward your device's aspect ratio — it never shrinks further to force a fit. If a page's content sits right at the edge of the detected box, check the live preview before downloading.

name: Is there a limit on how many pages I can optimize?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There's no page-count or file-size limit, and no per-hour task limit. Optimize a single-page PDF or a several-hundred-page book as often as you need.

name: Do I need to turn off grayscale for color pages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Grayscale is on by default since most e-readers are grayscale or E Ink displays, but you can turn it off if you're reading on a color tablet like a Boox Tab or want to keep color diagrams intact.

name: Is the E-Reader Optimizer completely free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree is free with no subscription, no daily or hourly limits, and no signup. No watermark is added to the output and there's no file size restriction.
